title: Authentication and authorization boundaries
description: Place auth checks at the right layer — middleware, server components, server actions, or client components — so private data stays private.

data.text: Authentication answers *'who are you?'*. Authorization answers *'what are you allowed to do?'*. In the App Router, you can enforce both at several layers: **middleware**, **server components**, **route handlers**, and **server actions**. The sooner you reject an unauthorized request, the less surface area you expose.

Middleware runs before every request hits your application code. It is the right place for redirects, cookie-based session checks, and geo or A/B rules. Server-side auth checks protect your data. Client-side checks improve UX by hiding UI, but they never protect secrets.

items: Middleware: redirect unauthenticated users before any page renders.
Server Component: fetch user-specific data and redirect if missing.
Server Action / Route Handler: enforce role checks before mutations.
Client Component: hide buttons or sections for UX, never for security.

data.title: Never rely on client-side auth
data.text: Any code shipped to the browser can be modified. Always validate sessions and permissions on the server. Client-side hiding is purely for user experience.

data.title: Server-side session check
data.content: Use getServerSession inside a Server Component.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Middleware is the first gate for route protection.
Server Components and Server Actions are the second and third gates for data protection.
Client-side hiding is only a convenience layer.
data.takeaway: Put auth checks as close to the data as possible, and remember that client-side checks are never a security boundary.
